story: story-042 — per-client setAsideBuffer added to skimSurplus

concernsEvaluated.label: Slippage-basis amplification under buffers
concernsEvaluated.rationale: minOut is derived on the pre-buffer `totalShares` while only `1-f` of the proceeds reach the recipient; the absolute slippage bound is preserved but recipient's fractional slippage = slippageBps / (1 - f) where f = totalBufferShares / totalShares. M-02's bounded-leak acceptance memo (project_reflax_nav_floor_tradeoff.md) was framed in terms of the recipient's tolerance to a `slippageBps * tradeSize` leak; under non-zero buffer fraction the same absolute leak is absorbed by a smaller principal, exceeding the recipient's bound.

concernsEvaluated.label: Aggregate buffer cap absence (no minimum recipient take)
concernsEvaluated.rationale: Per-client cap is 100% but no aggregate cap. Two clients of equal principal at 100% → totalBufferShares == totalShares → toRecipient = 0. No revert. Combined with M-02 amplification this is the boundary at which the recipient's fractional slippage tolerance becomes infinite (division-by-zero in the bound).

concernsEvaluated.label: Client front-runs skim (non-owner trigger check)
concernsEvaluated.rationale: Verified that the only writer to setAsideBufferSize is setSetAsideBuffer (onlyOwner). No other code path mutates it. The per-client safeTransfer in _distributeBuffer goes to clients[i] (protocol-owned contract address), but: (a) the parent skimSurplus carries nonReentrant; (b) underlying is a standard ERC20 per project convention (no ERC777 hooks). No non-owner can reconfigure the buffer mid-skim. The owner-acknowledged front-run quirk in the AUDITOR NOTE remains within the C-01 (centralization) envelope.

concernsEvaluated.label: Buffer state persistence across client removal/re-add
concernsEvaluated.rationale: setClient(client, false) removes the client from _authorizedClients but does NOT clear setAsideBufferSize[client]. A subsequent setClient(client, true) silently reactivates whatever buffer was last set (e.g. 100%). Operator footgun; within the trusted-owner model but a clear correctness gap on the setter contract.

concernsEvaluated.label: Recipient minOut bypass (integrator wires to wrong return)
concernsEvaluated.rationale: The function intentionally returns `toRecipient` under the buffered path (line 520), NOT the gross `underlyingReceived`. The IYieldStrategy NatSpec (line 90) and the AYieldStrategy NatSpec (line 354) both correctly document the return value as 'the actual underlying delivered to `recipient`'. Integrators applying a minRewardTokenSupplied floor against the function's return ARE protected by construction. Pattern-matcher PATTERN-001 was over-broad. No new finding.

concernsEvaluated.label: Buffer accounting vs vault NAV (storage destination of set-aside)
concernsEvaluated.rationale: The per-client buffer underlying is sent directly to clients[i] via underlyingToken.safeTransfer (line 516) — it leaves the strategy. It is NOT credited to clientBalances (principal is intentionally untouched) and it does NOT count toward the strategy's NAV after the skim. There is no double-counting. The intentional design is that the client contract holds the returned underlying as an idle reserve. A secondary observation: the buffered underlying earns no yield while held by the client (no auto-redeposit path); this is consistent with the AUDITOR NOTE's 'reserve against below-par dips' framing — not a defect.

concernsEvaluated.label: Sandwich profitability under amplified effective slippage
concernsEvaluated.rationale: An attacker's extractable value is governed by absolute slippage (≤ slippageBps * tradeSize), unchanged. What changes is the recipient's tolerance: their realized loss as a fraction of what they receive is amplified by 1/(1-f). From the attacker's side, no new primitive; from the protocol/recipient side, the M-02 acceptance bound is breached. Captured in ECON-001.

findings.title: Recipient's effective slippage tolerance is amplified by 1/(1-f) under non-zero aggregate buffer, breaching the M-02 bounded-leak premise
findings.description: story-042 derives the swap's `minOut` from the pre-buffer aggregate `totalShares` (line 434–435), then distributes the proceeds by sending the buffered slice (`totalSetAside`) to clients[] and only the remainder (`toRecipient = underlyingReceived - totalSetAside`) to `recipient`. Define `f = totalBufferShares / totalShares` (the aggregate buffer fraction). The slippage worst-case the swap admits is `Δ = idealUnderlying * slippageToleranceBps / 10000` absolute. Because the buffered clients receive their slice from the actual swap proceeds proportionally to `bufferShares[i] / totalShares`, the buffered clients absorb fraction `f * Δ` of the absolute slippage and the recipient absorbs `(1 - f) * Δ` — but the recipient also only receives `(1 - f)` of the principal. The recipient's fractional slippage is therefore `Δ * (1-f) / (idealUnderlying * (1-f)) = Δ / idealUnderlying`, which is unchanged in fractional terms only if buffered clients absorb their proportional share of slippage. HOWEVER, the implementation distributes proceeds proportionally to `bufferShares[i]` (line 513), so the slippage IS absorbed proportionally — but the recipient receives a smaller absolute principal. The key issue: the M-02 acceptance memo (`project_reflax_nav_floor_tradeoff.md`) frames the bounded-leak tolerance as `slippageBps * tradeSize` against the recipient's expected take. Under buffers, the recipient's expected take is reduced by factor `(1 - f)` while the absolute slippage bound on the *swap* is unchanged; if a downstream integrator's `minRewardTokenSupplied` floor was sized against the unbuffered expectation, the relative slippage exposure as a fraction of integrator yield is multiplied by `1/(1-f)`. At f=0.5 this is 2x; at f=0.9 this is 10x; at f=0.99 this is 100x. The accepted bound thus only holds at f=0 (the default).
findings.economicImpact: Recipient (typically a yield accumulator such as SYA) sees the same absolute slippage Δ amortized over a much smaller principal, so the effective drag on integrator yield scales as `slippageBps / (1 - f)`. Parametrically, the per-skim leak relative to recipient take = `slippageToleranceBps / (1 - totalBufferFraction)`.
findings.attackScenario: 1. Operator configures clients A and B with setAsideBufferSize = 90% each (f = 0.9). 2. Withdrawer calls skimSurplus(token, recipient). 3. Sandwich attacker observes the pending swap of `totalShares` and frontruns the pool to push the AMM rate to the worst-case allowed by minOut (slippageBps absolute). 4. The swap settles at minOut. 5. Recipient receives only (1-f) * minOut. The recipient's per-skim leak is the same absolute Δ but represents `slippageBps / (1-f)` of recipient's expected take.
findings.profitability: Bounded by `slippageBps * tradeSize` per skim, same as the unbuffered case in absolute terms. The amplification is *not* a new theft primitive — it is an enlargement of the integrator-facing slippage envelope beyond what the M-02 acceptance memo bounded.
affectedParties: recipient (typically stableYieldAccumulator) — sees amplified relative slippage
downstream LP/yield consumers reading the recipient's reported yield
findings.parametricBound: fractionalRecipientLeak <= slippageToleranceBps / (10000 - totalBufferFraction * 10000); at totalBufferFraction == 1 the bound becomes unbounded (toRecipient = 0 case, see ECON-002).
findings.recommendation: Three layered mitigations: (a) cap `slippageToleranceBps` to a meaningfully low ceiling (per L-01 — currently up to MAX_BPS=10000); (b) introduce an aggregate buffer cap (see ECON-002) so `totalBufferFraction` is bounded by design; (c) optionally derive `minOut` against the recipient's share, i.e. `minOut_recipient = (totalShares - totalBufferShares) * convertToAssets * (MAX_BPS - slippageBps) / MAX_BPS` and revert if `toRecipient < minOut_recipient` after the swap — this restores the per-recipient slippage bound regardless of `f`. Note: (c) may interact with M-02's NAV-anchored basis (still uses convertToAssets), so it does not by itself remediate M-02 — it ONLY restores the bound that M-02 was already accepted against.
findings.ledgerInteraction: AMPLIFIES M-02 (already acknowledged/by-design). The acceptance memo `project_reflax_nav_floor_tradeoff.md` framed the leak as bounded by `slippageBps * tradeSize`; story-042 invalidates that framing whenever any client has a non-zero buffer. Re-confirm the acceptance with the author OR adopt the parametric bound as the new acceptance statement.
references: src/AYieldStrategy.sol:241-251 (AUDITOR NOTE — acknowledges some economic quirks but not the slippage-amplification angle)

findings.title: No aggregate cap on per-client buffer percentages allows total set-aside to reach 100% of underlyingReceived, reducing recipient take to zero with no revert
findings.description: `setSetAsideBuffer` enforces `bufferPercent <= 100` per client (line 255). The sum of `setAsideBufferSize[client]` across the authorized-client set is not capped. When client principals are non-trivially distributed and multiple clients carry high buffer percentages, the aggregate buffer share `totalBufferShares` can approach `totalShares`, in which case `toRecipient` (line 518) collapses to zero and the entire swap output is redirected to clients[]. The skim then completes successfully with no revert, but the withdrawer's `recipient` parameter is effectively a no-op. Concretely: with two clients of equal principal both at `setAsideBufferSize = 100`, `totalBufferShares == totalShares`, `totalSetAside == underlyingReceived`, `toRecipient == 0`, and the safeTransfer at line 519 is skipped by the `if (toRecipient > 0)` guard.
findings.economicImpact: Recipient (and any downstream integrator pricing in expected yield from skimSurplus) sees zero proceeds despite the swap consuming all surplus value and incurring slippage. Underlying funds are not lost (they remain protocol-owned via the buffered clients) but the keeper / withdrawer / SYA expecting positive flow gets none.
findings.attackScenario: Operator configures all (or all but one weight-significant) authorized clients with bufferPercent = 100. The next skimSurplus produces toRecipient = 0. SYA (or other integrators) records zero yield for this period. No revert, no warning, no event flag distinguishing this from a no-surplus skim.
findings.profitability: Not an attacker primitive; it is an operator footgun / unsafe configuration. Combined with ECON-001, it is the boundary case where the recipient-fractional slippage bound becomes undefined (1/0).
affectedParties: downstream yield accumulators consuming the return value
findings.parametricBound: toRecipient = underlyingReceived * (1 - sum(principal[i] * setAsideBufferSize[i]) / (totalDeposited * 100)) (approximation, modulo per-client floor rounding). At sum-weighted buffer == 100%, toRecipient == 0.
findings.recommendation: Track an aggregate buffer-weight metric on `setSetAsideBuffer` calls and enforce a configurable ceiling (e.g. `aggregateBufferCapBps`), OR introduce a require in `_distributeBuffer` that `toRecipient > 0` (or `>= someMin`) when totalBufferShares > 0 so that an all-clients-at-100 misconfiguration reverts loudly rather than silently zero-returning. Per memory `feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md`, prefer revert-on-malformed-config rather than silent clamp.
findings.ledgerInteraction: Companion to ECON-001 — together they describe the slippage-bound failure mode under buffer mis-sizing. C-01 (centralization) still covers the owner-trust framing, but this is a setter-design gap orthogonal to centralization risk: even a benevolent owner has no defense against a fat-finger across clients.

findings.title: Removing a client from _authorizedClients does not clear setAsideBufferSize, so a subsequent re-add silently reactivates the previously-configured buffer
findings.description: `setClient(client, false)` calls `_authorizedClients.remove(client)` (line 189) but does NOT touch `setAsideBufferSize[client]`. If owner had previously set `setSetAsideBuffer(X, 100)` for client X, then later deauthorized X, the storage slot still reads `100`. A later `setClient(X, true)` reactivates X with `setAsideBufferSize[X] == 100` silently — the operator must remember to call `setSetAsideBuffer(X, 0)` before re-adding, or X's full surplus share will be set aside on the next skim. This is a config-coherence gap (not an exploit, the owner controls both setters), but it is a foreseeable operator mistake whose blast radius is captured by ECON-001/ECON-002. The static-analysis skipped-pattern note in pattern-matches.json acknowledges 'setAsideBufferSize being writable for not-yet-authorized client addresses is a stale-state surface' — this finding completes the symmetry: it is also a stale-state surface on the *deauthorize* side.
findings.economicImpact: Indirect: enables ECON-001/ECON-002 via operator error rather than malice. Owner-controlled; out-of-attacker-reach.
findings.attackScenario: Not an attack; an operator-error scenario. Sequence: 1) setSetAsideBuffer(X, 100). 2) setClient(X, false) (X deauthorized; buffer storage NOT cleared). 3) Time passes; X's buffer is forgotten. 4) setClient(X, true) re-adds X. 5) Next skimSurplus silently redirects X's full surplus share to X.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) clear `setAsideBufferSize[client]` inside the `_auth == false` branch of `setClient`, OR (b) gate `setSetAsideBuffer` on `_authorizedClients.contains(client) == true` (which would also resolve the writable-for-not-yet-authorized stale-state pattern flagged by the static-analyzer), OR (c) explicitly document that buffer state persists across deauthorize/reauthorize and rely on operator discipline. Option (a) is the strongest and aligns with the principle of least surprise; per memory `feedback_revert_over_silent_clamp.md`, prefer explicit state machinery to silent persistence.
findings.ledgerInteraction: Complements C-01 (centralization). On its own, QA-tier; bundled into the existing QA / ledger triage.
references: src/AYieldStrategy.sol:183-193 (setClient — does not clear buffer on remove)
reports/reflax-yield-vault-07/pattern-matches.json (skipped CENTRALIZATION-ADMIN note acknowledging the symmetric pre-auth gap)

noFindingExplanations.concern: C3 — non-owner front-run of buffer reconfiguration
noFindingExplanations.verdict: No code path lets a non-owner write to setAsideBufferSize; safeTransfer to clients[i] is non-reentrant (parent guard) and underlying is a standard ERC20 (no ERC777 hooks per project trust assumptions). The AUDITOR NOTE's owner-acknowledged front-run quirk stays within C-01.

noFindingExplanations.concern: C5 — recipient minOut bypass via wrong return value
noFindingExplanations.verdict: Author returns `toRecipient` (the post-buffer remainder) under the buffered path. Integrators wiring a minRewardTokenSupplied floor against the return value are protected by construction. PATTERN-001 over-flagged; reclassified.

noFindingExplanations.concern: C6 — buffer accounting vs vault NAV
noFindingExplanations.verdict: Buffer underlying leaves the strategy via safeTransfer to clients[i]. It is NOT credited to clientBalances and does NOT count toward strategy NAV after skim. No double-counting, no NAV inflation. Intended as an idle reserve at the protocol-owned client contract; consistent with the AUDITOR NOTE design framing.

ledgerReconciliation.M-02: AMPLIFIED by story-042 — ECON-001 documents the breach of the bounded-leak premise under non-zero aggregate buffer. Recommend either (a) re-confirming acceptance with the parametric bound `slippageBps / (1 - f)` in the memo, or (b) adopting the recommendation in ECON-001 to restore the original bound.
ledgerReconciliation.L-01: UNCHANGED by story-042; ECON-001's recommendation (cap slippageToleranceBps) is a layered mitigation that also resolves L-01.
ledgerReconciliation.L-02: UNCHANGED in asymptotic bound; story-042 doubles the constant factor (second loop + memory allocation) but does not change the per-iteration scaling. No new finding.
ledgerReconciliation.C-01: Amplified per the contract-profiler (setSetAsideBuffer is another owner power). ECON-003 documents an owner-error footgun within this envelope.

patternMatcherReclassifications: PATTERN-001 (slippage-basis-mismatch) reclassified — the return-value angle is a non-issue (author returns toRecipient correctly); the underlying basis-vs-distribution angle is captured in ECON-001 with a parametric framing.
